nodes.label: Express Trusts and Their Creation
nodes.summary: The three certainties (intention, subject matter, objects), formalities, constitution of trusts, sham and illusory trusts, and secret trusts.

nodes.label: The Three Certainties Overview
nodes.summary: A valid trust requires certainty of intention, subject matter, and objects (Knight v Knight). Failure on any certainty renders the trust void.

nodes.label: Certainty of Intention
nodes.summary: Imperative words must be used; precatory words (wish, hope, request) are insufficient. The court construes the document objectively to determine if a trust was intended.

nodes.label: Certainty of Subject Matter
nodes.summary: Tangible property must be segregated or clearly identified. For intangible property (e.g. shares of the same class), segregation is not required (Hunter v Moss).

nodes.label: Certainty of Objects (Beneficiary Principle)
nodes.summary: Fixed trust requires a complete list of beneficiaries. Discretionary trust requires conceptual certainty (is or is not test). A trust for purposes (non-charitable) is generally void unless an exception applies.

nodes.label: Formalities and Constitution
nodes.summary: Trusts of land must be evidenced in writing signed by the person able to declare the trust (Conveyancing and Property Ordinance Cap 219 s.5). A trust must be constituted by vesting the legal title in the trustee.

nodes.label: Sham Trusts
nodes.summary: A sham trust is one where the settlor intends to create only a facade of a trust, retaining actual beneficial ownership. Requires common intention between settlor and trustee to mislead third parties.

nodes.label: Illusory Trusts
nodes.summary: An illusory trust occurs where the settlor reserves such extensive powers that no real beneficial interest is alienated. The trust is invalid because it lacks substance.

nodes.label: Secret Trusts
nodes.summary: A trust created by a testator outside the will, binding the legatee on conscience, to avoid disclosing the beneficiary's identity. Requirements: intention, communication, and acceptance by legatee during testator's lifetime.

nodes.label: Fully Secret vs Half-Secret Trusts
nodes.summary: Fully secret trust: the will makes an absolute gift but the legatee holds on a communicated trust. Half-secret trust: the will shows the gift is on trust but does not name the beneficiary. Different timing rules apply to communication.

nodes.label: Hong Thai Citizens Travel Services Ltd v Hang Seng Bank Ltd [1993] 1 HKC 482
nodes.summary: Certainty of intention: advertising that funds were deposited for the possible benefit of customers showed no intention to create a trust. Also: customers too indefinite a class.

nodes.label: Fu Chuen Sang v Cheung Ching Tak [1961] HKLR 573
nodes.summary: Certainty of intention: testator's wish for his wife to adopt a son created no trust; precatory words insufficient.

nodes.label: Re London Wine Co (Shippers) Ltd [1986] PCC 121
nodes.summary: Certainty of subject matter: tangible bulk not segregated; no trust created over unascertained goods.

nodes.label: Re Goldcorp Exchange Ltd [1995] 1 AC 74 (PC)
nodes.summary: Certainty of subject matter: unallocated gold bullion; no proprietary interest passed. PC affirming London Wine.

nodes.label: Hunter v Moss [1994] 1 WLR 452
nodes.summary: Certainty of subject matter: intangible shares of the same class do not require segregation for a valid trust.

nodes.label: Re CA Pacific Finance Ltd [2000] 1 BCLC 494
nodes.summary: HK application of Hunter v Moss: intangible assets not requiring segregation. Needs paragraph verification.

nodes.label: JSC Mezhdunarodniy Promyshlenniy Bank v Pugachev [2017] EWHC 2426 (Ch)
nodes.summary: Sham trust: deeds allowing settlor to freely exercise powers for his own benefit held to be a sham. Needs HK application verification.

nodes.label: Re Chu Wai Tung (a bankrupt) (No 2) [2013] 5 HKLRD 202
nodes.summary: Illusory trust: living trust allowing grantors to exhaust assets during their lifetime created no present trust for the son.

nodes.label: Clayton v Clayton [2016] NZSC 30
nodes.summary: Illusory trust: trust invalid where settlor retained rights indistinguishable from absolute ownership. Persuasive authority for HK.

nodes.label: Webb v Webb [2020] UKPC 22
nodes.summary: Illusory trust: settlor retained powers inconsistent with alienating beneficial interest. Persuasive authority for HK.

nodes.label: Tsang Tat Hung v Tsang Tat Wing [2005] 3 HKLRD 24
nodes.summary: Secret trust: mother intended second son to co-own flat only as manager on secret trust for youngest son. Requirements of intention, communication and acceptance discussed.

nodes.label: Verify HK Secret Trust Cases and Formalities
nodes.summary: Research and verify HK cases on secret trusts (fully secret and half-secret), formalities under Cap 219 s.5, and constitution of trusts.
